distr discrete¶

Families for counts and other integer-valued variables. Each page documents one family: the parameters, the support, how to evaluate the density and the distribution function, how to draw samples, and, for the families that have one, the object form and the maximum-likelihood fit.

The Surface¶

Family

What it is

Bernoulli

The Bernoulli distribution: a single trial with two outcomes, success with probability p and failure otherwise.

Bessel

The Bessel distribution: a discrete distribution whose masses are proportional to the terms of a modified Bessel function series.

Binomial

The binomial distribution: the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials with the same success probability.

Geometric

The geometric distribution: the number of independent trials needed to obtain the first success.

Hypergeometric

The hypergeometric distribution: the number of successes in a sample drawn without replacement from a finite population.

NegativeBinomial

The negative binomial distribution: the number of failures before the r-th success, and the standard model of over-dispersed counts.

Poisson

The Poisson distribution: the number of events in a fixed interval when events occur independently at a constant average rate.

Rademacher

The Rademacher distribution: the values +1 and -1, each with probability one half.

Skellam

The Skellam distribution: the difference of two independent Poisson counts, a distribution on the integers that can be negative.

Yule

The Yule–Simon distribution: a discrete power-law distribution with a heavy tail, the model of preferential attachment.

Zeta

The zeta (Zipf) distribution: a discrete power-law distribution on the positive integers.
